about: Stage R12 (docs/staging/r12-prereg.md section 2): the class of every condition in front of an offer() of src/sim/candidates.ts, a reading of the code by the stage's author; scripts/r12-offer-table.ts merges it into the table by the condition's text. c: PHY physical, PER perceptual, SOC social fact, ADV advice, QUO quota or timer, DIC dice, SWI switch. w: plain words. adult: always or never true of an animal aged 8 or over. is: the base fact a switch equals. off: a base fact that takes the condition out. fix: keep, drop or rules. line: the packet line that carries the fact when the condition is dropped. needs: with fix drop, what the drop waits for (body: body outcomes allowed as a teacher; wild: only the pairs a wild choice record covers; absent: the rules value every option the rule cut). over, at a site: a condition that reads differently there. rulings: short is the one-sentence form for the two-minute page. sites: print is the hash of the site's gating as it was classified.

rulings.title: The dividing line itself.
rulings.short: Is a condition a "social fact" when it only says whom an act is addressed to, and "advice" once it says who may act, toward whom or when? I recommend yes; every count here follows from it.
rulings.ask: Is it right to call a condition a "social fact" when it only says who the act is addressed to (a community member, its mother, the animal that just charged it, a female in oestrus), and "advice" as soon as it says who may act, toward whom or when (the direction of rank, an age, a sex, a balance of numbers, a threshold)?
rulings.recommend: yes. Every count on this page follows from that line; a different line moves conditions between the two columns without changing a single rule.

rulings.title: Which tree.
rulings.short: May the model choose which tree to travel to, among up to eight the animal sees or remembers, instead of the one the rules' ranking leaves? I recommend yes.
rulings.ask: May the model choose which tree to travel to among trees shortlisted by what the animal sees and remembers, instead of being shown the one tree left of the four the rules value most?
rulings.recommend: yes. It is the largest choice no model has ever made (about 51 trees possible, one shown), and the rules value every tree, so a scaffold teacher exists. The shortlist's own numbers are counted as hand-set.

rulings.title: Trees no animal has itself seen.
rulings.short: Should it also be offered trees from its community's list that it has never seen? I recommend not yet, counting how often the rules go to one.
rulings.ask: Should the model also be offered trees from its community's list, which no single animal remembers?
rulings.recommend: not in the first build: its own view and memory only, with a count of how often the rules themselves travel to a listed tree. If that count is large, add one slot labelled "known to my community".

rulings.title: Which water, and drinking when not thirsty.
rulings.short: May it choose which water to drink at, and be offered a drink when not thirsty? I recommend yes to the first; the second only once the body's acts have a teacher other than the rules.
rulings.ask: May a drink be offered at any remembered water whenever one is remembered, instead of only when the thirst gauge is above zero and only at the one water the rules value most?
rulings.recommend: the choice of water: yes. Offering a drink without thirst: only once a teacher that is not the rules exists for the body's acts (forked body outcomes, the ruling deferred on 10 October); until then that rule stays and is counted.

rulings.title: Nesting and sheltering whenever possible.
rulings.short: May nesting and sheltering from rain be offered whenever possible? I recommend the same condition as for drinking, and keeping "no new nest in full daylight".
rulings.ask: May "build a nest" and "shelter from the rain" be offered whenever physically possible, instead of only when the rules' own value says so (the nest's value above 0.25, the body colder than neutral)?
rulings.recommend: as for water: yes once a body-outcome teacher is allowed, counted until then. Keep the light condition on starting a nest (none in full daylight): an earlier stage offered nests at any light and day nests took a third of the daytime.

rulings.title: Whom to groom.
rulings.short: May any community member in reach be offered as a grooming partner, whatever it is doing? I recommend yes where wild records can teach the choice (today an adult male among adult males); elsewhere "only a settled partner" stays.
rulings.ask: May any community member in reach be offered as a grooming partner, whatever it is doing, instead of only those resting, grooming, sheltering or nursing?
rulings.recommend: yes, where a teacher that is not the rules can teach the choice, and only there. Wild records of whom a male grooms are in hand (Ngogo: an adult male among the adult males present); Taï's are approved for download and count once checked. For every other pair "only a settled partner" stays a rule and is counted: a model taught by the rules would learn it back.

rulings.title: Whom to greet.
rulings.short: Should "pant-grunt only to a dominant" stay a rule? I recommend keeping and counting it, and letting the model choose which dominant.
rulings.ask: A pant-grunt is offered only toward an animal that outranks the greeter, and only toward the one such animal the rules score highest. Should the direction rule stay?
rulings.recommend: keep "only to a dominant" for now and count it: no wild record of greetings is in hand, so a model taught by the rules would learn the same rule from its labels. Let the model choose which dominant. The direction of greetings then stays true by construction and may not be credited to the model.

rulings.title: Strangers: the rules on numbers.
rulings.short: Should the numbers rules for strangers stay (charge only with 3 males and 2 more than theirs)? I recommend keeping and counting them.
rulings.ask: A charge at strangers needs at least 3 males of one's own and 2 more than theirs; with fewer, the only options are to display, call back or retreat, each by its own count. Should these stay rules?
rulings.recommend: keep and count them. The acts are rare and dangerous, no teacher exists, and the counts are already shown to the model as facts.

rulings.title: Courtship rules.
rulings.short: Should the courtship rules stay (guarding only from the top two ranks; mating only 1.5 hours after his last)? I recommend keeping and counting them.
rulings.ask: Guarding a female is offered only to the top two ranks, a consortship only to a male who is not the alpha and has a bond with her, coercion only toward a female near full swelling, and mating only 1.5 hours after the male's last copulation. Should these stay rules?
rulings.recommend: keep and count them. The quota has a built replacement (the paternity mechanism, off on the working base); adopting it is a decision about the base, not about the menu.

rulings.title: Dice.
rulings.short: Should the three acts opened by a random roll (gang attack, attack on an infant, transfer) stay with the rules? I recommend yes.
rulings.ask: A gang attack, an attack on an infant and a female's transfer to another community are opened by a random roll and then offered at a fixed high score. Should they stay with the rules?
rulings.recommend: yes. They stay hazards, decided by the rules and reported as the rules' acts. No record can teach a once-in-a-lifetime act, and an untaught model would set its rate by accident.

staysShort: Everything for animals under 8; the three acts opened by a roll; the age line of 12 for aggression, courtship, hunting, patrols, calls and displays; the rules that open every social act (the model chooses among what they offer); the timers after events and "not at night"; and, outside this table, when an act ends, how long a bout lasts and the 25 choices inside execution.
stays: Every act of an animal under 8. The rules decide for them (about a quarter of all decision points), and every result says so.
The acts opened by a roll (gang attack, infanticide, transfer): the rules open them and the rules decide them.
The age line of 12. Aggression, courtship, hunting, patrols, calls and displays are offered only from 12: an animal of 8 to 11 on the model is never shown them. Kept and counted.

Every contest, coalition, courtship, hunting, patrol, sharing and repair act: it stays on the model's menu behind the rules that open it today, each rule counted as hand-set. The model chooses among what is offered; no teacher but the rules exists for offering more.

Timers. The windows after an event (about 2 minutes to answer a threat, 0.3 h to answer a call or to reconcile) and the "once per event" marks stay as numbers and are counted. The cooldowns after aggression and display are already out on the working base.
"Not at night": the light conditions on party following, displays, aggression and avoidance stay.

Inside `offer()` itself, so in front of every place and not counted per place: an option the rules score at −0.4 or below is not offered; each act keeps one to three targets by the rules' score; and an animal on a silent patrol is offered no call and no display (the patrol's silence, on in the working base). The design says which of these go for which acts (`docs/staging/r12-prereg.md` §5.4).

Outside this table, in other files: when an act ends, how long a bout lasts, the 25 choices made inside execution (the nest tree, the patrol's route, who captures, the mother's refusal to nurse, calls on arrival), contest outcomes, and who is alerted to a conflict.
